lessons.title: Modeling UI State with Sealed Interfaces
lessons.content: A sealed interface/class restricts a type hierarchy to a known, closed set of subtypes, letting the compiler enforce exhaustive `when` blocks - if you add a new state and forget to handle it in the UI, the build fails instead of crashing at runtime. Real scenario: instead of a fragile combination of isLoading: Boolean, error: String?, and data: List<Item>? fields (which allows impossible states like isLoading=true AND error != null simultaneously), model the screen as one sealed hierarchy where only one state can exist at a time.

lessons.title: Sealed Classes for Domain Errors (avoiding stringly-typed errors)
lessons.content: Instead of throwing generic Exceptions or returning error strings, model domain errors as a sealed hierarchy - this makes error handling exhaustive and testable, and lets different layers react differently to different failure types (e.g. retry on NetworkError, prompt re-login on AuthError, but not on ValidationError). Real scenario: a repository layer returning a sealed Result type instead of throwing, so the ViewModel can pattern-match on exactly what went wrong without parsing exception messages.
